suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-21 adds this relationship only as the user-approved bounded clinical proposition. The cited review describes insulin resistance as a major contributor to the pathogenesis of type 2 diabetes and a key part of its associated metabolic abnormalities. Require a clinically established insulin-resistance syndrome phenotype and separately diagnosed type 2 diabetes with compatible chronology; the review addresses a central pathophysiologic component but does not establish that insulin resistance alone caused any individual's diabetes or that all insulin-resistant phenotypes progress to diabetes. Preserve beta-cell dysfunction, genetic susceptibility, obesity and adiposity, medications, endocrine disease, pancreatic disease, secondary diabetes, and other metabolic contributors. Do not infer type 2 diabetes from insulin resistance markers alone. The cited literature supports only this constrained proposition and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The review identifies insulin resistance as a major contributor to type 2 diabetes pathogenesis, supporting a bounded pathophysiologic association for research rather than an individual causal conclusion.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation under 38 CFR section 3.310 is established by the current evidence; the guard explicitly limits the claim to an association requiring individual metabolic and etiologic review.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Reduced insulin responsiveness can impair glucose uptake and increase compensatory insulin demand, while progressive beta-cell dysfunction may permit hyperglycemia and type 2 diabetes; this remains a population-level pathway, not individual proof.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. Insulin resistance is a major pathophysiologic contributor, but the source does not establish that insulin resistance alone caused an individual's diabetes or resolve the contribution of beta-cell, genetic, adiposity, medication, endocrine, pancreatic, and secondary causes.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Independent diagnoses, objective metabolic phenotype, diabetes classification, compatible chronology, and evaluation of competing contributors remain necessary for individual assessment.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: pancreatic disease or other secondary diabetes
